describes: A slab step of split slate (port step 2b, R2b; reference 06): a slab the stair's rise thick laid on its bed, its top a bedding plane; its front and open ends split across the laminae, each lamina a little in or out of the next; its nosing rounded unevenly by weather and the feet, here and there a flake of the top lost so the lamina beneath shows; its corners knocked; its tread worn by the record's feet. Rigid: the flight sets it, settled, and never bends it. Fitted to its step's facts: its length between its ends (joint, walled or open), the rise, the going and the lap.

laminae.note: R2b: the laminae a step's split front shows, [count, weight] (reference 06: one to three layers in each riser).

laminaLeastMm.note: R2b: no lamina thinner than this.

frontPointMm.note: R2b: the front's points along the step, this far apart: its line wanders between them.

frontPointsMost.note: R2b: at most this many points along the front, a lost piece's included (the thinnest gaps thinned first): with four laminae L0 stays under its 300 triangles on a 2.3 m slab.

frontWanderMm.note: R2b: how far the front's line wanders in or out of straight (reference 06: no nosing runs straight).

frontWanderStepMm.note: R2b: the most it wanders from one point to the next.

laminaOutMm.note: R2b: each lamina's front in or out of the step's line by up to this: the line of light or shadow between laminae.

laminaOutStepMm.note: R2b: a lamina's offset wanders along the step by up to this from point to point, so the line between laminae comes and goes (reference 06).

laminaFlushShare.note: R2b: where a lamina's offset is under this share of its most, it is flush with the next: no line there.

laminaJitterMm.note: R2b: and each of its points a little more.

laminaWaveMm.note: R2b: the beds between laminae not quite level, by up to this.

endSlant.note: R2b: an end's slant in plan, as a share of the step's depth, by its end.

endOutMm.note: R2b: each lamina's end in or out by up to this, by its end.

knockMm.note: R2b: the top lamina's front corner knocked off, along each edge, by its end.

lossChance.note: R2b: the share of steps with a piece of the top lamina lost from the nosing, the lamina beneath showing (reference 06).

lossMm.note: R2b: that piece's length along the nosing.

lossDepthMm.note: R2b: and how far back it goes.

lossThickMm.note: R2b: the lost piece a flake of the top this thick, its own lamina (reference 06: the treads' broad shallow steps where the top flaked).

lossPoints.note: R2b: the break's back line through this many points.

lossRagged.note: R2b: the break's back line an arch, deepest in its middle, each point back this share of it: a flake breaks off ragged, not stepped.

lossEdgeMm.note: R2b: the break's ends, split back on a slant over this.

nosingMm.note: R2b: the nosing's round, weathered, before the feet's wear (reference 06: every nosing rounded).

nosingVary.note: R2b: the round at each point of the nosing, this share of the step's: weather rounds a nosing unevenly (reference 06).

breakRoundMm.note: R2b: where a piece of the top lamina was lost, the break's arris barely rounded: a break is sharper than the weathered nosing.

roundPerWear.note: R2b: the nosing rounded further by this times the wear the feet took there.

endRoundMm.note: R2b: an end's top arris rounded, by its end.

topRowsMm.note: R2b: the top's rows back from the nosing, where the feet wear it; then the moss's row and the next riser's line.

mossRowMm.note: R2b: the row this far in front of the next riser, where moss holds.

chamferMm.note: SN4: every exposed arris chamfered, a seeded leg of 10 to 12 mm per stone, at least 2 px at 8 m through the 28 mm lens.

chamferMeasure.note: Measured along each face, as a mason gives it (C10); 'face' (the chamfer's width) is not built.

arrisMaxDeg.note: Two faces meeting at a turn of 20 degrees or more meet at an arris (a face's own facets never do: they are one face).

riserFacets.note: SN4: a riser's planes, weighted [count, weight]: at most three; most risers one plane, one in four broken back once.

endFacets.note: An open end's planes, weighted [count, weight].

facetStepMm.note: SN4: a facet stepped back 15 to 25 mm (a seeded whole mm) where laminae broke.

facetLeastMm.note: SN9: no face under 50 mm; every facet is a lamina at least this high.

chipPerMille.note: An open end's top front corner knocked, per mille of stones (SN4: most stones none).

chipLegMm.note: A knock's three legs, least and most: at least SN9's 50 mm, so a chip is no sliver.

skirtMm.note: A drawn face runs this far past a hidden face or a cover: the next riser's foot set back (facetStepMm's 25) and SN9's 3 mm contact, checked at build.

nosingReachMm.note: The nosing's rounding runs back this far (stair_stages.py: the nose band).

wearGridMm.note: SN4: the wear's grid columns at most 120 mm apart across the walking line.

wearFlatShare.note: Per mille of a level's error (the kind's, kinds/stair.json): wear under this is flat stone.

l1WearShare.note: Per mille of L1's error (the kind's, kinds/stair.json) the wear's grid may take at L1; the chamfer's sagitta is the rest, elsewhere on the stone. At L1's 11 it is 5.5 mm.

patches.note: The face patches (blender/parts/stone/slate/patches.manifest.json; SN6) each kind of face draws one from by seed: the tread from the bed patches, a split face from the split ones, a bed face from the bed ones.

note: Sizes from the stair kind (kinds/stair.json) and R1's walling table (packs/stavanger-1989/walling.json, the dry-split-1874 working's steps): w the finish's slab widths (other: 700 to 2300), h the block's stone rises (150 to 180) with the rise error (12), d the going's range (270 to 400) with the steps' lap (40 to 60). Levels (R2b): L0 is at most 292 triangles by construction (nine front points, four laminae; 62 to 262 measured over three seeds of 14 steps on a 2.3 m flight), under SN8's 300. L1 is L0: its laminae, its lost flake, the wear's rows and its round's middle facet each show from 6 to 18 m in low sun (without only that facet, 1.1 to 5.6% of the flight's pixels change by more than 3 L*; reviews/lt1/port/2b/r2b/step/switch-d9-l0-round1facet-diff.jpg). R2a's params (chamferMm to patches) are stones.py's, which the gully's export builds until slabstep.py is wired in. L2 to L4 are the chunk's (the port's step 5), so none is made here. The part's own numbers are its params, each with its reason; the material's (wear, the corner's break) are materials/slate.json's, the working's (laps, joints) walling.json's (reviews/lt1/port/2b/r2a/stones/blender.md, Data and code).
